text:
The major product (P) in the following reaction is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In alcoholic KOH the methyl ketone forms an enolate at its terminal $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ group. The CHO group is attached to a quaternary ring carbon, has no α-hydrogen and can act only as an electrophile.

This enolate can close a six-membered ring onto either the CHO carbon or the ring C=O carbon. The aldehyde carbonyl is the more electrophilic of the two, so intramolecular aldol addition occurs at the CHO group.

The new six-membered ring contains the former CHO carbon, the quaternary ring carbon (now a spiro carbon), the two $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ groups, the side-chain C=O carbon and the former $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ carbon.

Acid and heat dehydrate the β-hydroxy ketone to the α,β-unsaturated ketone, so the C=C forms between the former CHO carbon and the former $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ carbon, conjugated with the side-chain C=O, while the ring ketone is retained.


[IMG]

Attack on the ring ketone would give the fused bicyclic enone with an angular CHO (option C), but the ketone is the weaker electrophile.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Outermost electronic configuration of a group 13 element, E, is $4s^{2}, 4p^{1}$. The electronic configuration of an element of p-block period-five placed diagonally to element, E is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An outer configuration $4s^{2}4p^{1}$ in group 13 belongs to period 4, so E is gallium (Ga, $Z=31$).

The element placed diagonally to Ga in period 5 lies one period down and one group to the right, that is group 14 of period 5: tin (Sn, $Z=50$). Indium ($5p^{1}$) lies directly below Ga, not diagonally.

Tin follows krypton with the filled $4d$ subshell, so its configuration is $[\text{Kr}]4d^{10}5s^{2}5p^{2}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text: Which one of the following species doesn't have a magnetic moment of 1.73 BM, (spin only value)?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Species does not have a magnetic moment of 1.73 BM means species must not contain single unpaired electron.

(a) Molecular orbital configuration of O${}_{2}^{+}$ (15 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{1}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{o}}^{\ast }$

Unpaired electron = 1

$μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{1(1+2)}=\sqrt{3}=1.73$

where n = no. of unpaired $e^{-}$

$\therefore$ $μ$ = 1.73 BM

(b) CuI $\Rightarrow$ $Cu^{+}$ $-$[Ar]$3d^{10}$, Unpaired electron = 0

$I^{-}$ $\to$ [Xe], unpaired electron = 0

Therefore, $μ$ = 0

(c) [$Cu(NH_{3})_{4}$]$Cl_{2}$

$Cu^{2+}$ $\to$ [Ar]$3d^{9}$

Unpaired electron = 1,

Therefore, $μ$ = 1.73 BM

(d) Molecular orbital configuration of $O_{2}^{-}$ (17 electrons) is 

$σ_{1s^{2}}σ_{1s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2s^{2}}σ_{2s^{2}}^{\ast }σ_{2p_{z}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}=π_{2p_{y}^{2}}π_{2p_{x}^{2}}^{\ast }=π_{2p_{y}^{1}}^{\ast }$

Unpaired electron = 1

Therefore, $μ$ = 1.73 BM

Therefore, CuI does not have magnetic moment of 1.73 BM.

text: The hybridisations of the atomic orbitals of nitrogen in NO${}_{2}^{-}$, NO${}_{2}^{+}$ and NH${}_{4}^{+}$ respectively are.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hybridisation = Number of sigma bonds + number of lone pair of electrons + number of coordinate bond.

For $NO_{2}^{-}$ hybridisation = 2 sigma NO bonds + 1 lone pair on N = 3; so $NO_{2}^{-}$ is $sp^{2}-$hybridised.

 
[IMG]

For $NO_{2}^{+}$ hybridisation = 2 sigma NO bonds = 2; so $NO_{2}^{+}$ is sp-hybridised.

 
[IMG]

For $NH_{4}^{+}$ Hybridisation = 4 sigma NH bonds = 4; so $NH_{4}^{+}$ is $sp^{3}-$hybridised.


[IMG]

Therefore, hybridisation of N in $NO_{2}^{-}$, $NO_{2}^{+}$, $NH_{4}^{+}$ are $sp^{2}, sp, sp^{3}$ respectively.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text: $Cu^{2+}$ salt reacts with potassium iodide to give
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Iodide ion is oxidised by $\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}$ to iodine, while copper(II) is reduced to copper(I), which precipitates as white copper(I) iodide:

$2~\mathrm{Cu}{}^{2+}+4\mathrm{I}{}^{-}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}{}_{2}\mathrm{I}{}_{2}+\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$

With a copper(II) salt such as copper sulphate and potassium iodide:

$2~\mathrm{CuSO}{}_{4}+4\mathrm{KI}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Cu}{}_{2}\mathrm{I}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{K}{}_{2}\mathrm{SO}{}_{4}+\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$

Copper(I) iodide is written as $\mathrm{Cu}{}_{2}\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$, as in these equations, or by its empirical formula $\mathrm{CuI}$; both formulas stand for the same compound, the product of the reaction. Hence option (A), $\mathrm{Cu}{}_{2}\mathrm{I}{}_{2}$, and option (C), $\mathrm{CuI}$, are both correct.

$\mathrm{Cu}{}_{2}\mathrm{I}{}_{3}$ (with copper in a non-integral oxidation state of $+1.5$) and $\mathrm{Cu}(\mathrm{I}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ are not formed in this reaction.

Hence, the correct options are (A) and (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

text:
The wavelength of electrons accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 40 kV is x $\times$ $10^{-12} m$. The value of x is $___________. ($Nearest integer)

Given : Mass of electron = 9.1 $\times$ $10^{-31} kg$

Charge on an electron = 1.6 $\times$ $10^{-19} C$

Planck's constant = 6.63 $\times$ $10^{-34} Js$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Wavelength of electron is given by

$λ=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$

Here q = charge on electron, V = potential difference

$λ=\frac{6.63\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2\times 9.1\times 10^{-31}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 40\times 10^{3}}}$

$=\frac{6.63\times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{1164.8\times 10^{-47}}}=6.144\times 10^{-12}\approx 6\times 10^{-12}$

x = 6

OR

$λ=\frac{12.3}{\sqrt{V}}A^{o}$

$=\frac{12.3}{200}=6.15\times 10^{-12}$ m

$\therefore$ Ans. is 6
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 20th July Evening Shift

50M

10 M
